title: Celerity Claims Proxy — field notes and integration action list
content:
One-pager capture from 2025-09-22 call with Celerity Insurance (technical + product leads). Purpose: capture integration constraints, expected load profile for claims triage proxy, initial SLOs, and immediate action items. Draft for internal alignment before solutions-eng scoping.

Attendees (call):
- Sarah Kim (Celerity, Head of Claims Automation)
- Dev: Marco Ruiz (Celerity)
- IT/Sec: Denise Park (CISO, Celerity)
- Redwood: Asha Patel (AM), Liam Chen (solutions-eng), Sofia Martinez (SRE consult)

Quick summary:
Celerity wants a lightweight inference "proxy" in front of their legacy claims intake pipeline. The proxy will handle: extraction of key fields from uploaded PDFs/images, short conversational clarifications (2–3 follow-up Qs), and a classification/routing decision (severity: low/med/high) with a short human-friendly rationale. The initial goal is to reduce manual triage by ~30% for P1 intake hours and provide structured metadata to downstream systems. They’re leaning toward a private deployment (VPC) with optional on-prem agent for PHI-handling regions.

Business constraints & priorities:
- Data residency: US-only for PHI claims; EU customers separate (phase 2).
- Compliance: must integrate with their KMS (HashiCorp Vault) and produce audit logs for every inference decision.
- Latency target: median end-to-end (request → classification) <= 300ms for 90th percentile during business hours; fallbacks acceptable to a lower-fidelity model for brief spikes.
- Throughput: expected steady-state 20 r/s (peak 80 r/s for 30–45m during morning intake). Typical payloads include multi-page PDFs (OCR step upstream) plus extracted text; core LLM prompt length ~600 tokens average, worst-case 2k tokens.
- Cost sensitivity: they want guidance on model / quantization tradeoffs; primary objective is < $0.015 per inference on average (target), but accuracy regressions >2% on routing not acceptable.

Technical constraints noted in call:
- Current infra: hybrid cloud (GCP primary, private DC for PHI).
- They run an internal message bus (Kafka) and expect the proxy to publish structured events; request/response over HTTP + auth via mTLS.
- KMS: HashiCorp Vault for keys; Redwood must either call Vault via their VPC peering or we provide a KMIP-compatible agent.
- No external model API calls allowed for PHI traffic — must be fully private or use a certified private gateway.
- Obs/Tracing: they require correlation ids (X-Correlation-ID) propagated, and sample-level token-level cost breakdown for audits.

Integration gotchas / risks (from notes):
1) OCR variability: not all upstream attachments will have uniform OCR quality. Need a confidence cutoff for short-circuiting to human review and a fallback pipeline to request manual review.
2) Token estimates: downstream token count can spike with long descriptions or embedded transcripts — we need robust prefix trimming and a pre-tokenizer to detect problematic inputs.
3) KMS latency: if Vault calls are in the critical path, 90th pct latency may exceed target. Consider local short-lived key cache or a sidecar approach.
4) Network topology: on-prem air-gapped DCs will likely need an on-prem runtime bundle; plan for an offline deploy path and a lightweight update mechanism.
5) Audit log size: token-level logs for every inference will generate significant storage — propose configurable retention and sampled cost logs to meet compliance and cost goals.

Initial model / runtime recommendations (rough):
- Candidate models: a distilled instruction-following model for classification + a small chat context model for clarifications. For routing decisions prefer 7B/8B Q8* quantized variants on dedicated GPUs for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Runtime: Redwood Private deployed in their VPC with a dedicated pool for PHI routes; set an autoscale policy for peak 100 r/s buffered at 1.5x to avoid throttling.
- Batching: enabled only for background bulk jobs; for latency-critical routing set max batch size = 1–4 and adaptive batching window 10–20ms.
- KV cache: use prefix caching for common claims templates to save cost; add a cache miss metric to alert on cache cold starts.

Observability & evals:
- Define 3 eval prompt sets: routing accuracy (binary), rationale quality (human-eval subset), and clarification adequacy (completion rate for 2-step dialogs).
- Instrument token-level cost per request, per-model; expose daily aggregates to customer.
- Create a canary route: 5% traffic to new model/profile with automatic rollback if routing accuracy drops >1.5% over 24h.

Proposed rollout phases (timeline sketch):
- Week 0–2: scoping & infra access (VPC peering, Vault read-only test account), sample payload capture (1k items).
- Week 3–4: private runtime PoC (dev env) integrated with Kafka sink + test webhooks, basic dashboard.
- Week 5–7: pilot with 10% production traffic, monitoring hooks, manual review queue integrated.
- Week 8–12: ramp to 100% with phased canaries and post-launch QA.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- AM (Asha): gather regulatory contact and PHI boundary doc from Celerity — ETA 2025-09-25.
- Solutions (Liam): prepare PoC infra checklist + list of required ports/peering, include Vault access patterns — ETA 2025-09-29.
- SRE consultancy (Sofia): draft sidecar design for local key caching and failure modes — ETA 2025-10-02.
- Celerity (Marco): provide 1k redacted sample payloads with OCR output and labels for routing — ETA 2025-09-26.
- Security (internally): run initial threat model for the on-prem bundle + acceptance criteria for updates — ETA 2025-10-06.

Open questions to resolve on next call:
- Can Celerity accept sampled token logs (e.g., 10%) for audit purposes or do they require all token-level logs indefinitely?
- Which Vault API patterns are supported (AppRole vs. transit-only)? Need specific endpoints and sample IAM policy.
- Expected SLA for feature work vs. incident response (they asked about 24/7 support options for PHI incidents).
- Clarify fallback policy: do we return a low-confidence routing to human ops or a best-effort model classification?

Customer sentiment & negotiation points:
- Positive: strong interest in private deploy and Redwood’s traceability features. They were explicitly happy with our canary/rollback suggestions.
- Concern: cost target vs. accuracy — they prefer accuracy but have strict budgetary bands; we should prepare a cost/accuracy sensitivity matrix for the next meeting.

Notes for proposals doc (what to include in the draft SOW):
- Clear boundaries for PHI traffic and deployment topology by region.
- Vault integration approach and responsibilities for key rotation.
- SLA/uptime targets + incident response terms for PHI classifications.
- Pricing structure: pilot fixed-fee + usage-based after ramp, with a 3-month performance review and cost-tuning checkpoint.

Misc small gotchas (quick):
- Their Kafka cluster uses topic-level ACLs; our PoC needs a service account with least privilege.
- They use an old PDF metadata header format; include a parser for legacy X-Form fields.
- Timezone: heavy traffic at 08:30–09:15 local (PST).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Set up follow-up technical deep-dive (solutions + infra + security) — propose 60–75m slot.
2) Request 1k sample payloads + redaction checklist from Marco.
3) Internal sync to decide candidate runtime profile and prepare initial cost sensitivity sheet (Liam + Finance consult).

——
Notes appended 2025-10-02 after internal sync:
- SRE suggests we design a small local key cache using short-lived ephemeral keys from Vault; this reduces KMS latency risk and simplifies audit trails.
- Finance flagged that $0.015 average/inference is aggressive for on-prem PHI handling; suggested to present 3 tiers (low-cost quantized, mid-accuracy, high-accuracy non-quantized) with per-inference ranges and sample monthly bill estimates at expected volume.
- Added an extra action: security to confirm whether token-level logs must include full text or just token counts + deltas (impact on compliance/storage).

End of scratchpad. Keep this as working doc — will convert to scoped SOW and Jira tickets after next deep-dive.
comments: Liam: will prototype sidecar pattern this week (ETA 09/29)
Sofia: recommend sampled token logs (10%) by default — pending security sign-off
